(I might have made some thread for this a few years ago, but the situation has changed so I'd like to make a new one.)

We have two independent typeclasses which separately imply IsBot 0, these being docs#CanonicallyOrderedAdd and docs#LinearOrderedCommMonoidWithZero. There are a bunch of different convenience lemmas we can prove with this assumption, such as 0 < x ↔ x ≠ 0, 0 ≤ x ↔ x = 0, x < y → 0 < y, etc. Annoyingly, we have some of these for one typeclass but not the other. I would like to make a new mixin IsBotZeroClass to collect all of these.

A benefit of this is that we'd be able to generalize a bunch of theorems that are currently stated for CanonicallyOrderedAdd, but which truly require only the IsBot 0 assumption (see e.g. file#Mathlib/Algebra/Order/SuccPred for examples). This would be convenient to me, given that the types CGT#NatOrdinal and CGT#Nimber in the CGT repo are of this form. Currently I just have a big and ugly macro to copy those theorems from docs#Ordinal.
I had the impression that this class already existed! So yes, given that there are positive usecases for this class, let's add it.
I'll make a PR for this soon, I'd just like to get #38148 out of the way first.

Implementation wise, I suppose we should just go for an instance from docs#CanonicallyOrderedAdd to IsBotZeroClass and an extends IsBotZeroClass line in the definition of docs#LinearOrderedCommMonoidWithZero. There's no reasonable way to add IsBotZeroClass as an assumption to docs#CanonicallyOrderedAdd or docs#LinearOrderedCommMonoidWithZero (and the latter should probably be unbundled sometime soon, since deep inheritance chains are quite slow).
